memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The Lord will cause you to be defeated before your enemies. You will come at them from one direction but flee from them in seven, and you will become a thing of horror to all the kingdoms on earth... The Lord will afflict you with the boils of Egypt and with tumours, festering sores and the itch, from which you cannot be cured. The Lord will afflict you with madness, blindness and confusion of mind." — Deut 28:25-28 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice how these curses are the exact reversal of the earlier blessings. Where obedience would scatter their enemies in seven directions, now Israel themselves would flee in seven. Where they would have been the head, now they would become "a thing of horror." God's discipline was a precise undoing of every blessing they forfeited. Diseases, tumours, even madness and confusion of mind are named. It is a bleak and painful list.

Passages like this are meant to shake us, and they should. But they also reveal how seriously God takes the covenant relationship, and how devastating it is to abandon Him. The horror described here is not God being cruel; it is the terrible weight of a people cutting themselves off from the fountain of all good.

We can be grateful, and rightly so, that this covenant of curses is not the word spoken over those who are in Christ. Yet we should not read these verses with cold detachment. They show us what our sin deserves. Every one of us has rebelled against God in some measure, and a holy God cannot simply overlook it.

This is precisely why the cross is such staggering good news. At Calvary, the horror our sin deserved fell on Jesus instead. He was made "a thing of horror," despised and rejected (Isa 53:3), so that we could be welcomed and healed. The darkness of this passage makes the light of the gospel blaze all the brighter.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I grasp the seriousness of sin as God does?
2. How does this dark passage deepen my gratitude for the cross?
3. Am I resting in Christ, who bore what my sin deserved?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Holy God, these warnings show me how serious sin truly is. Thank You that Jesus bore the horror I deserved so I could be healed and welcomed. I rest in His finished work. Amen.
